chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Humran ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
He said: "And those who disbelieve, their guardians are the tyrants"
And those who disbelieve, their guardians are the tyrants

key_terms.التَّحْرِيفُ: Alteration or substitution, referring to the change in the Quranic text.
key_terms.الطَّاغُوتُ: The tyrant (singular), the original word according to the narration.
key_terms.الطَّوَاغِيتُ: The tyrants (plural of Taghut), here noted as a substitution in the Quranic text.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the word substitution in the verse regarding the guardians of disbelievers?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) utilizes the verse 'And those who disbelieve, their guardians are the tyrants' to discuss textual variations, specifically noting the substitution of the singular 'al-Taghut' with its plural form 'al-Taghut' in certain recitations. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the fluidity of the Quranic text (Tahreef) and the authority of the Imams in clarifying the true meaning behind these linguistic shifts.
